phone-gimbal: Handheld 3-axis stabilizers that hold a smartphone steady and can follow a subject.

products.name: Hohem iSteady V3 Ultra AI Tracking Phone Gimbal, 400 g payload, touchscreen remote
specs: About 9 h balanced; 4–5 h with AI tracking and fill light
Separate 2 MP AI camera on a magnetic light module; works with any camera app
Detachable 1.22-inch touchscreen remote with live tracker view
products.returns: 7 days from receipt, unused and in original packaging, with prior approval from store@hohem.com; buyer pays return shipping unless the fault is Hohem's
products.summary: A folding 3-axis phone gimbal rated for 400 g of phone, 100 g more than DJI, Insta360 and Zhiyun allow, in a 428 g body with a built-in tripod and selfie stick.
products.fit: Owners of Pro Max and Ultra phones who keep the case on and sometimes add a MagSafe lens, mic or light.
caveats: We could not confirm a maximum phone thickness in the specs we read. Foldable owners should choose the M7, which lists 12.5 mm.
SLR Lounge found the clamp only just strong enough for big phones in thick cases. Some phones may need the case off.
The AI tracker is a separate camera beside the phone, so its framing can differ from what the phone records.
Reviewers saw a 2.5-star Google Play rating for the Hohem Joy app. Tracking and recording work from the remote without the app.

products.name: Hohem iSteady M7 AI Tracking Phone Gimbal, 500 g payload, foldable-phone clamp
specs: Up to 12.5 mm (0.49 in), including folded foldables
Up to 12 h; about 8 h with the AI tracker
Detachable 1.4-inch touchscreen remote, about 32 ft range
Magnetic fill light, warm to cool white plus RGB
products.returns: 7 days from receipt, unused and in original packaging, with prior approval from store@hohem.com; buyer pays return shipping unless the fault is Hohem's
products.summary: Hohem's heavy-duty phone gimbal: rated for 500 g and folded phones up to 12.5 mm thick, with a touchscreen remote and an app-free AI tracker.
products.fit: Owners of foldables like the 11.3 mm iPhone Duo, and anyone running a phone with a cage, lens and mic.
caveats: Big and heavy: about 1.6 lb with its tripod, and not pocketable.
Its clamp tops out at 90 mm wide, narrower than the V3 Ultra's 98 mm.
The Gadgeteer counted 18 controls and found the remote's preview did not match the phone's framing.
The Hohem Joy app had a 2.3-star App Store rating when reviewed. It is needed for firmware updates and some modes.

notes: Query choice: Google autocomplete (US) suggests 'gimbal for heavy phone', 'best gimbal for heavy phone(s)', 'gimbal for foldable phone', 'gimbal for iphone 18 pro max' and 'gimbal for iphone duo'. Today's answers are thin: SEO roundups (gimbalreview.com mentions an 'iPhone 16 Flip' and has internal contradictions; thewearify) and forum threads. Pain points, counted from what I read: (1) phone too heavy or thick for the clamp, about 10 mentions (gimbalreview, accessorytested, two MacRumors threads, a kentfaith review, a DJI forum post, DJI's case-thickness FAQ, D1Store on Fold fit, SLR Lounge clamp strength, Insta360's drop warning); (2) gimbal bulk, 6 (PetaPixel, TechRadar, gimbalreview, Notebookcheck, CGM, Camera Jabber); (3) Hohem Joy app, 4 (Gadgeteer 2.3 stars on iOS, Notebookcheck 2.5 on Google Play, ProVideo Coalition on app limits, CGM: app needed for firmware); (4) AI-tracker framing offset, 3 (Notebookcheck, Gadgeteer, ProVideo Coalition). Segments and winners: heavy phone in a case plus add-ons goes to the V3 Ultra (400 g vs rivals' 300 g, 428 g body); foldables and 400-500 g rigs go to the M7 (500 g, 12.5 mm folded thickness, verified on CGM, and the store's Creator Kit text says 500 g for large and foldable phones); iPhone under 300 g wanting the lightest kit and DockKit goes to the Insta360 Flow 2 Pro (Amazon/maker only, not linked per the temporary rule). Phone data from Apple's compare page: iPhone 18 Pro Max 249 g, 78.0 mm wide, 8.75 mm; iPhone Duo 254 g, 84.1 mm wide, 11.3 mm closed. DJI OM8: 170-300 g, 67-84 mm, 6.9-10 mm (dji.com); DJI says no official US sales. The OM8P (11 mm) had no US pricing at launch, so it was left out. Prices: the Hohem store product endpoints returned HTTP 429 all session (storecheck product and WebFetch), so I could not read variants. Store search, the home page and /pages/black-friday-deals all showed V3 Ultra at $124.99 sale ($189 regular, Black/White, 400 g payload, touchscreen remote, AI tracking) and M7 at $215.99 sale ($299 regular) on 2026-11-17. The store ships to the US from a US warehouse, with free standard shipping over $64. Returns are 7 days and the gimbal warranty is 1 year (store policy page). Unverified and kept off the page: the V3 Ultra's maximum phone thickness (12.5 mm in TechRadar and PetaPixel snippets only), the Zhiyun Smooth 5S AI's width and thickness (50-90 mm and <10 mm in snippets only), Insta360's US price ($159.99 in snippets), the M7's exact bare weight (629 g in snippets), and Pixel 10 Pro Fold thickness (10.8 mm in snippets). Codes: CJ gave HOHEM10OFF and LM40 with no terms. A 2025 blog tied HOHEM10OFF to a September 2025 10% sale. The store prints no code today, only an 8% email-signup offer and accessory bundle savings. Both codes still need cart testing.
